unit.unitOverview:
Say what colour a thing is.
Say if it is big or little.
Put the describing word BEFORE the thing.
A red bag. A big box.
unit.learningPath:
Listen to the lesson.
Words: colours and sizes.
Patterns: the describing word comes first.
Listen to three short texts.
Describe things out loud.
Write about three things.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
functions: Ask and say what colour a thing is
Say if a thing is big or little
Put a describing word before a thing
Ask which one a person means
Say a thing is good or bad
unit.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

visual.lectureScript:
This is Unit 7. Today, colours.
In Unit 6 you named a thing. A bag.
Now you say more. A red bag.
First, the colours. Listen.
Red. Blue. Green. Yellow.
Say them with me. Red. Blue. Green. Yellow.
Black. White. Brown.
Say them with me.
Now, size. Big and little.
A big box. A little box.
Long and short. New and old.
Now the important part. Word order.
In English the describing word comes first.
We say: a red bag.
We do not say: a bag red.
Listen again. A big box. A new pen.
The colour or the size, then the thing.
In many languages it is the other way.
So this one needs practice. Say it many times.
A red bag. A big box. A new pen.
And the question. What colour is it?
It is red. Or: it is a red bag.
Both are right.
Last, two useful words. Good and bad.
This is a good pen. That is a bad pen.
That is Unit 7. Go and describe things.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: The describing word comes FIRST
grammar.explanation:
This is the big one today.
English puts the describing word before the thing.
Many languages do the opposite.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
a red bag        NOT a bag red
a big box        NOT a box big
a new phone      NOT a phone new

a + describing word + thing
a + red + bag
grammar.workedExample:
You have a bag and it is black.
1. Start with a.
2. Then the colour: black.
3. Then the thing: bag.
4. Say: a black bag.
5. Check the order: a, colour, thing.
grammar.commonMistake:
This is the most common word-order mistake.
No: I have a bag red.
Yes: I have a red bag.
Say it out loud many times until it feels normal.
grammar.practice:
Put them in order.
1. bag / a / blue
2. box / big / a
3. phone / a / new
4. door / green / a
5. table / a / little
6. book / a / good
grammar.answerKey:
1. a blue bag
2. a big box
3. a new phone
4. a green door
5. a little table
6. a good book
Five or six right? This is the pattern of the unit.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: What colour is it?
grammar.explanation:
One question, two good answers.
Both are right. Use the short one when you are quick.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
What colour is it?
It is red.
It is a red bag.

What colour is your bag?
Black.
It is black.
It is a black bag.
grammar.workedExample:
Someone asks about your coat.
1. They ask: What colour is your coat?
2. Short answer: Blue.
3. Longer: It is blue.
4. Longest: It is a blue coat.
5. All three are correct English.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not say: It is colour blue.
The word colour is in the question only.
Yes: It is blue.
grammar.memoryTip: A one-word answer is fine here.
grammar.practice:
Answer about things near you.
1. What colour is your pen?
2. What colour is the door?
3. What colour is this page?
4. What colour is your bag?
grammar.answerKey:
Any true answer is right.
Check: did you leave out the word colour?
It is blue. Not: It is colour blue.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Big, little, and the others
grammar.explanation:
Size words work the same as colours.
They come before the thing.
They also come after is.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Before the thing:  a big box    a little bag
After is:          The box is big.    The bag is little.

big / little
long / short
new / old
full / empty
grammar.workedExample:
Your room is not large.
1. The word is little.
2. You can say it two ways.
3. Before the thing: a little room.
4. After is: My room is little.
5. Both are correct.
grammar.commonMistake:
After is, you do NOT need a.
No: The box is a big.
Yes: The box is big.
grammar.memoryTip: Two places: before the thing, or after is.
grammar.practice:
Write the sentence two ways.
1. box / big
2. bag / little
3. street / long
4. phone / new
grammar.answerKey:
1. a big box / The box is big.
2. a little bag / The bag is little.
3. a long street / The street is long.
4. a new phone / The phone is new.
All four? You can describe a thing two ways.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Which one?
grammar.explanation:
When there are two or more, you need which.
It is the question that stops a mistake.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Which one do you want?
The red one, please.

Which bag is yours?
The little one.

which = there is more than one
what = you do not know at all
grammar.workedExample:
There are two bags and one is yours.
1. You are asked: Which bag is yours?
2. Do not say the whole thing again.
3. Say the describing word and one.
4. Say: The black one.
5. Or: The little one, please.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not say: The black.
English wants the word one after it.
Yes: The black one.
grammar.practice:
Answer each one.
1. Which bag? (the red one)
2. Which box? (the big one)
3. Which pen? (the new one)
4. Which door? (the green one)
grammar.answerKey:
1. The red one.
2. The big one.
3. The new one.
4. The green one.
All four? You can pick one thing out of many.

red ... blue ... green ... yellow
black ... white ... brown

teacherNotes.note: A red bag, not a bag red. Many languages put the describing word after the noun, so this is not carelessness — it is the learner's own grammar showing through. It needs saying out loud many times, not explaining twice. Pattern 1 and Practice 3 are where the time should go.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.note: The colours themselves are easy and most learners half know them already. They are here because they are the safest words to hang the word-order pattern on: the learner can see whether they are right without knowing any grammar.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: The black one, not the black
teacherNotes.note: English insists on the word one after a describing word used alone. It sounds like a small thing and it is the difference between sounding like a beginner and sounding fluent in a shop.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: Two describing words have an order too
teacherNotes.note: Size before colour: a little black bag, not a black little bag. Speaking 6 touches it. Do not make a rule of it here — a learner who gets one word in the right place has done what this unit asks.

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: blue — Blue is the colour of a clear sky.

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: green — Green is the colour of grass and leaves.

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: It is red. — The word colour stays in the question. It is red is enough.

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Which one? — Which is for choosing between things you can see.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: a red bag — The describing word comes before the thing.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: a big box — Size, like colour, comes before the thing.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: a new phone — a, then the describing word, then the thing.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: full — Full means there is no more space in it.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: short — Short is the opposite of long. Little is the opposite of big.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: one — English wants the word one after the describing word.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: very — Very big is bigger than big.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: good and bad — Good and bad are opposites. The others are not pairs.
